comment: The test suite's checks. See tools/suite/README.md for the fields; run-suite.ps1 runs them.

checks.name: build
checks.note: the build succeeds and its warning count (as a full build would print it) does not grow

checks.name: cik
checks.note: check_tiki_against_cik.py: model bounds and radius against the retail engine's .cik caches (742 of 743 match; lochnar's cache was written from animation files the archives lack, see docs/known-differences.md)

checks.name: tiki-parse
checks.note: cachealltikis on the client loads every .tik; its warnings and errors do not grow

checks.name: shader-parse
checks.note: viewmap on all 30 maps in a row (the renderer parses every shader a map uses, and ten and more map loads in a row survive); its warnings do not grow

checks.name: spawn
checks.note: compare.ps1: what the game module prints while the map spawns, against retail's dedicated server; the console's warnings and errors per map do not grow

checks.name: state
checks.toleranceWhy: pending events come from random choices the game seeds from the clock; retail differs from itself as much
checks.note: compare-player.ps1: level variables and pending events ten seconds after the player enters, the headless test player against the retail client; not under (see shots)

checks.name: entities
checks.note: every entity's whatis ten seconds in

checks.name: walk-jump
checks.note: walks, jumps, lands and stops; the test player reads 4 to 6 units short of retail (known-differences.md, With scripted input)

checks.name: gaspod-down
checks.note: the gas pod must not park in Julie's chest (the trace owner rule)

checks.name: fstrafe-fast
checks.note: fstrafe with both games at com_maxfps 250: ours barely moved Julie at high frame rates (about 30 units short) until the client stopped sending a command from frames the limiter runs at once, in which every key reads as up (CL_CreateNewCommands). The tolerance is 8, not 3: ours sleeps between frames where retail spins, so its frames at 250 are uneven and Julie ends up to 5 units ahead of retail (docs/known-differences.md, Frame pacing and movement commands)

checks.name: doors
checks.note: opens every door with the sound trace on; the probe must finish (read the fastpneu.wav lines in the logs)

checks.name: h2e
checks.note: homes2evil's doors, one at a time, with the sound trace on

checks.name: shots
checks.toleranceWhy: maps with an entry cinematic or moving scenery at three seconds vary by a point or two between runs
checks.note: one screenshot three seconds after entry on every map but under, where the probe's waitforplayer never returns on either game (its intro sets the player's model)

checks.name: crosshair
checks.toleranceWhy: the probe aims with +lookdown for a fixed time, so its pitch, and the whole view, varies with frame timing from run to run

checks.name: fx-guns
checks.toleranceWhy: the probe aims with +lookdown for a fixed time, so its pitch, and the whole view, varies with frame timing from run to run
checks.note: the whole game end to end; demo-guns plays this scene frame by frame from retail's demo

checks.name: fx-range
checks.toleranceWhy: the probe aims with +lookdown for a fixed time, so its pitch, and the whole view, varies with frame timing from run to run
checks.note: the whole game end to end; demo-guns plays this scene frame by frame from retail's demo

checks.name: fx-melee
checks.note: the whole game end to end (the gas pod lands where our server puts it); demo-melee plays this scene frame by frame from retail's demo

checks.name: shotgun
checks.toleranceWhy: the probe aims with +lookdown for a fixed time, so its pitch, and the whole view, varies with frame timing from run to run
checks.note: the whole game end to end; demo-guns plays this scene frame by frame from retail's demo

checks.name: rocket
checks.toleranceWhy: the probe aims with +lookdown for a fixed time, so its pitch, and the whole view, varies with frame timing from run to run
checks.note: the whole game end to end; demo-guns plays this scene frame by frame from retail's demo

checks.name: muzzle
checks.toleranceWhy: a muzzle flash lives 0.05 s, so whether a shot catches one varies; two runs of one build differed by up to 10 points
checks.note: a flash lives 0.05 s, so which shots catch one varies from run to run

checks.name: chimney
checks.note: fakkhouse's centre chimney smoke rising through the sky brush over the house (a portalsky surface writes no depth); starts on intro and moves to fakkhouse by gamemap, since a startup +map fakkhouse on retail gives way to the startup intro

checks.name: demo-zoo
checks.note: retail's demo of a fight on zoo (two creepers, chaingun, rockets, Julie's death) played frame by frame on both games: the same snapshots, so what differs is the client side (renderer, client game module, HUD)

checks.name: demo-swamp1
checks.note: retail's demo of swamp1's opening cinematic, then Julie walking and firing rockets, played frame by frame on both games

checks.name: demo-muzzle
checks.note: muzzle's scene from retail's demo at 20 frames a second: the uzi's flashes through two cameras, in the same frames on both games

checks.name: demo-crosshair
checks.note: crosshair's scene from retail's demo: the shotgun's crosshair on the wall and then the floor, at the pitch retail reached

checks.name: demo-flashes
checks.note: the scenes of probe-muzz2 to probe-muzz5 (no longer checks of their own) from one retail demo at 20 frames a second: the chaingun's, hand gun's, shotgun's and rocket launcher's flashes beside the barrel, the uzi's beside its muzzle and its casings on the floor

checks.name: demo-guns
checks.note: the scenes of fx-guns, fx-range, shotgun and rocket from one retail demo at 10 frames a second: each gun fired at the floor ahead (flashes, tracers, puffs, holes, the crossbow's bolt, flames, the soul sucker's beam, the shotgun's grenade, a rocket's explosion and blast mark)

checks.name: demo-melee
checks.note: the scenes of probe-pfade, probe-fx-melee and probe-sword from one retail demo at 20 frames a second: a centre print's whole fade-in, the electric sword, axe and chain sword swings, a flashbang, a gas pod's cloud, the green and fire swords' swipes

checks.name: demo-hud
checks.note: the scenes of probe-flash, probe-ammofl and probe-pot (no longer checks of their own, nor is pfade or sword) from one retail demo at 20 frames a second: the health and water gauges' and the ammo bars' whole flashes, and the targeting reticle on an autoaim pot

checks.name: demo-slime
checks.note: retail's demo of Julie through a camera before, while and after she is coated in the anti-Sucknblaugh juice (a juice pond's slime): her skin with the slime drawn over it (RF_CUSTOMSHADERPASS), where ours drew the slime alone and left a faint outline of her

checks.name: demo-flash
checks.note: retail's demo of the colour a hurt sentient flashes (RF_LIGHTOFFSET): Julie hurt by slime (green) and lava (red), a creeper hurt (red) and poisoned (green); then Gruff's cigar tip glowing with his animation's entcolor commands (rgbGen fromentity)

checks.name: demo-invisible
checks.note: retail's demo of an Invisible Grawlix on fog beside the map's -300 light: an invisible model is lit only by lights of negative intensity, which light nothing else

checks.name: frametime
cfg: {each} viewmap {map}; wait 100; com_speeds 1; wait 400; com_speeds 0; echo ==== frametime {map}
checks.toleranceWhy: the medians are 0.2 to 0.7 ms (thousands of frames a second), where machine load alone moved cemetery from 0.2 to 0.4-1.1 ms on one build; a slowdown worth catching is several ms
checks.note: the median frame time on viewmap's camera on three heavy maps, uncapped; a sharp rise fails

checks.name: timedemo
checks.toleranceWhy: as frametime: the frames take a millisecond or two, which machine load alone moves by a large fraction; a slowdown worth catching is several ms
checks.note: the demo checks' retail demos with timedemo 1, uncapped: the mean frame time of each, without its first 20 frames; a sharp rise fails, and so does a demo that does not play to the end

checks.name: menus
checks.note: capture-menus.ps1: the .urc menus with no map loaded, against retail's

checks.name: widescreen
checks.toleranceWhy: the entry cinematic's moving camera (shot 0) lands a little differently in the two runs: 0.46% and 1.32% of pixels in two runs, where a 3D view that stops widening differs on 45%; the other shots and the saved game 0.08% to 0.19%
checks.note: probe-wide at 1280x720 and at 960x720, ours only (retail ran at 4:3): each wide shot's middle against the 4:3 shot below the HUD, and the two saved game pictures; both match when the 3D view keeps the 4:3 view's height (cl_widescreenFov) and the 2D layer its shape (cl_widescreenHud)

checks.name: menu
checks.toleranceWhy: shot 3 is the main menu 8000 frames after the push, so when it is taken depends on the frame rate, and the menu's animated clouds with it: alone, runs of one build gave 12.55, 13.03, 13.74, 15.29 and 15.47 against retail (2026-10-30, with and without a change that cannot reach it) while differing from each other by about 1% of pixels

checks.name: menu-clicks
checks.note: the main menu's buttons by their commands (load/save, controls, options and advanced options, credits, back, then New Game's 'map intro'), with no crash

checks.name: menu-back
checks.toleranceWhy: the clouds move between the two games' shots
checks.note: Back on the video and audio page: three shots from five frames after popmenu 1 (ours' screenshot shows a frame a few behind the interface), paired with retail's, which shows the main menu whole on the next frame (ours had faded the page out over black and the main menu in after it)

checks.name: skipcine
oursCfg: vpad queue "wait 1000; screenshot; echo ==== skipcine done; quit"
checks.note: Escape during training's entry cinematic: ours presses the key (vpad; the skip lands after the config's own lines, so the rest is queued behind it), retail types skipcinematic, which the key sends on both (0x41fb56); the shot is Julie's own view at the intro node once the skip thread has ended the cinematic (ours waits in frames, retail in ms)

checks.name: intro
checks.note: the startup intro with developer 0, from pictures of the window 5.3, 10.3 and 16 s after the game starts: the Ritual logo held, the Gathering logo held, the main menu (retail starts its intro about a second later than ours; these land in both holds). A config's waits would hold the intro up, which runs through the same command buffer

checks.name: save-load
checks.note: save-load.ps1: a save made 3 s in, loaded in a new process, against the game it saved (132 of 133 entities and one level variable differ, from the game module)

checks.name: lsload
checks.note: loads fakkhouse0004 and opens the main and load/save menus over it (the renderer's crash on the menu's first frame); needs that save in the player's home

checks.name: fdiag
checks.toleranceWhy: a miss or two at the player's entry and at the first step, timed by frames
checks.note: walks Julie onto fakkhouse's hovercraft and counts the client game module's prediction misses: a model's fractional top, packed into whole units, had her predicted falling the fraction and put back every snapshot (cg_exactbounds; docs/known-differences.md, Standing on a model)

checks.name: chain
checks.note: the level chain: gamemap through the whole game on the real client, each level loaded, autosaved and the inventory carried, against retail's run of the same

checks.name: restart
checks.note: vid_restart, snd_restart (sound on, volume 0) and ten map changes in a row on the client, each level entered before the next

checks.name: map-rush
checks.note: the restart check's map changes, each started 60 frames after the last, before the player has entered
